messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "The two auxiliary tasks used in the ESMM architecture for CVR modeling are CTR and CTCVR." -- cites: E3 (Section 1): quote "In ESMM, two auxiliary tasks of predicting the post-view click-through rate (CTR) and post-view clickthrough&conversion rate (CTCVR) are introduced."
2. "The ESMM architecture for CVR modeling includes a CTR network and a CTCVR network." -- cites: E4 (Figure 2): observation "The figure shows two sub-networks: CVR network and CTR network."

Cited evidence:
[E3] (text, Section 1, page 2): been well addressed in the scenario of CVR modeling, and none of above methods exploits the information of sequential actions. In this paper, by making good use of sequential pattern of user actions, we propose a novel approach named Entire Space Multitask Model (ESMM), which is able to eliminate the SSB and DS problems simultaneously. In ESMM, two auxiliary tasks of predicting the post-view click-through rate (CTR) and post-view clickthrough&conversion rate (CTCVR) are introduced. Instead of training CVR model directly with samples of clicked impressions, ESMM treats pCVR as an intermediate variable which multiplied by pCTR equals to pCTCVR . Both pCTCVR and pCTR are estimated over the entire space with samples of all impressions, thus the derived pCVR is also applicable over the entire space. It indicates that SSB problem is eliminated. Besides, parameters of feature representation of CVR network is shared with CTR network. The latter one is trained with much richer samples. This kind of parameter transfer learning [ 7 ] helps to alleviate the DS trouble remarkablely.
[E4] (figure, Figure 2, page 2) (image attached): Figure 2: Architecture overview of ESMM for CVR model- ing. In ESMM, two auxiliary tasks of CTR and CTCVR are introduced which: i) help to model CVR over entire input space, ii) provide feature representation transfer learning. ESMM mainly consists of two sub-networks: CVR network illustrated in the left part of this figure and CTR network in the right part. Embedding parameters of CTR and CVR net- work are shared. CTCVR takes the product of outputs from CTR and CVR network as the output.
Words printed in the figure: Concatenate � Concatenate CVR-task features Main Task Auxiliary Tasks pCVR pCTR pCTCVR � Embedding Layer Field-wise Pooling Layer MultiLayer Perception item field user field item field user field CTR-task features Shared Lookup Table element-wise + element-wise + element-wise x � � � [image]

verdicts.reason: The evidence in E3 (Section 1) states that in ESMM, two auxiliary tasks of predicting the post-view click-through rate (CTR) and post-view clickthrough&conversion rate (CTCVR) are introduced. This directly supports the claim.

The evidence in E4 (Figure 2) shows that ESMM includes two sub-networks: CVR network and CTR network. This supports the claim that the ESMM architecture for CVR modeling includes a CTR network and a CTCVR network.
